questions.answer: SQLite often runs inside the application; MySQL and PostgreSQL commonly run as separate server processes.
questions.explanation:
SQLite often runs inside the application; MySQL and PostgreSQL commonly run as separate server processes.
Why: SQL is a query language, not a database. SQLite, MySQL, and PostgreSQL are database management systems (DBMSs) that accept SQL. The SQLite project began in 2000; it needs no separate server and stores data in a file, so it is used in mobile and desktop apps, browsers, and devices. MySQL emerged in the 1990s and became common for web applications and servers handling many concurrent connections. PostgreSQL began as the POSTGRES project at Berkeley in 1986, led by Michael Stonebraker; SQL was added to the project in 1994, and the PostgreSQL name was adopted in 1996. It is used for server and analytics workloads requiring extensive SQL features and reliability. The systems share core SQL ideas, but data types, functions, administration commands, and some syntax differ.
